original_text:
You are given a PySpark DataFrame named web_traffic with the following schema:
| user_id | page_url | session_id | timestamp | 

user_id: Unique identifier for each user.
page_url: The URL of the page visited by the user.
session_id: Unique identifier for each browsing session.
timestamp: The timestamp of the page visit.

Your task is to write a PySpark program to:
Identify the top 3 most visited pages (page_url) across all users.
For each of these top 3 pages, calculate the average number of unique users visiting the page per session.
Sample Input:
+---------+-------------------+------------+-------------------+
| user_id | page_url | session_id | timestamp |
+---------+-------------------+------------+-------------------+
| 1 | /home | A | 2025-05-18 10:00 |
| 2 | /home | A | 2025-05-18 10:05 |
| 1 | /about | B | 2025-05-18 10:10 |
| 3 | /home | C | 2025-05-18 10:15 |
| 3 | /contact | C | 2025-05-18 10:20 |
| 4 | /home | D | 2025-05-18 10:25 |
| 4 | /about | D | 2025-05-18 10:30 |
| 5 | /home | E | 2025-05-18 10:35 |
| 5 | /contact | E | 2025-05-18 10:40 |
+---------+-------------------+------------+-------------------+

Sample Output:
+------------+----------------------+
| page_url | avg_users_per_session |
+------------+----------------------+
| /home | 1.75 |
| /about | 1.50 |
| /contact | 1.50 |
+------------+----------------------+
